title: Online play - House of Pips Wiki
description: Playing House of Pips online through Steam: inviting a friend, matchmaking, modes and loadouts, turn clocks, reconnecting, surrendering, ranks, rewards and leaderboards.
html:
Online play

Multiplayer on the main menu plays one opponent through Steam. The match is played at the host's table: the host's background, domino skin and music. Your own volume and mute settings stay your own.

What you need #

  • Steam running, on a Windows PC or a Steam Deck.
  • Nana's tutorial completed, like every other mode.
  • Both players on the same version of the game, or you won't see each other's lobbies.
  • The demo doesn't include online play.

Test builds #

To try a testing build, open the game's Steam Properties → Game Versions & Betas and select testing. Both opponents need the same Steam application and game version. Steam Playtest includes the full game's content, but its lobbies are separate from the full game's lobbies.

Three ways to play #

  • Invite a friend opens a private lobby with voice and typed chat. You choose the mode, send a Steam invite, and start the match once your friend shows as connected. Only the host can start.
  • Find a match searches the modes you selected for up to 30 seconds.
  • Quick match searches every mode for up to 60 seconds.

If nobody is found, the game offers to widen the search to all modes. Matchmade games pick the host at random and start automatically after a short countdown, which you can cancel. Play again after a match returns you both to the lobby.

Receiving an invitation #

A friend's invitation plays a short chime and lights a glowing envelope at the top of the screen, including while you are playing solo. Click the envelope to see the friend's Steam name and avatar, plus the invitation's date and time in your local time zone using AM/PM. If the sent time is unavailable, the panel shows when you received it instead.

  • Save and join saves your current solo table or draft before entering your friend's lobby. After leaving multiplayer, Continue resumes that solo match. If saving fails, your current match stays open and you do not join.
  • Join lobby enters the lobby when you have no active solo match. A solo match already saved in Continue remains available. Joining leaves any waiting lobby you are currently in.
  • Later, Esc, or controller Back keeps the invitation available while you carry on playing. Decline dismisses it.

Finish an action before saving and joining. Cutscenes and other foreground choices keep the envelope unavailable until they finish. An invitation cannot replace a live online match, and blocked players' invitations stay hidden.

Modes and loadouts #

Choose your modes with Choose game modes. Each mode card says whether it is playable online. Some modes are solo-only.

Online matches give both players equal loadouts instead of your career:

  • Old School: no skills, perks or supplies, just dominoes.
  • Other modes: both players play at level 30 with a separate online skill build and starting supplies you choose. Use Build skill loadout and Choose starting supplies. Your single-player skills are not affected.
  • Max skills gives both players every skill at its maximum rank and full perk access, first to 250.

Online drafts can offer any perk the mode allows, legendary perks included, whatever either player has unlocked in single-player.

Preparing each hand #

Both players choose their pre-hand items at the same time. Use an owned Boneyard Lantern, Hammer Wax or Dealer's Dare, then click Ready. An item you use shows Selected for this hand. You can finish your choices while your opponent is still choosing. The deal begins when both players are ready.

If you have no items to use before the hand, the screen explains that. Click Continue when you are ready, then wait for your opponent.

Playing at the table #

Online matches use the same mouse, keyboard and controller controls as solo play. See Controls, controllers and Steam Deck.

When Stumble requires a draw, the game draws for you before you play. A message names the Malus and its sound plays. If another draw effect offers a choice of revealed bones, you still choose which to keep. If the boneyard is empty, you can play a bone instead.

After confirming Pip Shift or Pip Shuffle, play that exposed bone before selecting another bone or visiting the boneyard. You can still rotate it and choose a matching open end.

If a choice is unavailable, an explanation appears on the table. You can make another valid choice and carry on with the same match.

Clocks #

  • Each turn has a 60-second clock. If it runs out, the player who ran out of time loses the match.
  • Drafts and hand setup give each player 120 seconds for their own choices. If time runs out, the game takes the default draft card or confirms Ready with the pre-hand items you have already chosen.
  • The clocks pause while a player is reconnecting.

Disconnects, surrendering and leaving #

  • If a connection drops, the match waits. Each match allows two minutes of reconnecting in total, shared across every drop. The screen counts it down.
  • If that allowance runs out, the match ends with no win or loss recorded.
  • Surrender concedes the match: it counts as a loss.
  • Leave match interrupts it without a win or loss.
  • Rage quit in Settings concedes the match.

Rank, level and rewards #

Your online profile shows a casual rank and an online level from your finished matches.

  • Wins raise your rank; losses and connection losses lower it. Matchmaking prefers opponents of a similar rank. Rank tiers run from Boneyard through Ivory, Brass and Gold to Delirium.
  • Your online level only goes up: a win earns more online XP than a loss, and interrupted matches earn none.
  • Online rewards are cosmetic only: tile backs, edge finishes, placement effects and badges such as First Table, Ten Wins and Comeback.
  • Finishing an online match earns the Across the Table achievement.

Standings and history #

  • Leaderboards rank players by wins in three groups: public presets, private presets and Custom matches. View them worldwide, around your own position, or among your friends.
  • History lists every opponent you've finished a match against.
  • You can block a player from the lobby or your history. Blocked players never appear in your searches and can't invite you.

Voice chat #

Private lobbies include voice chat. The Voice chat tab in Settings sets the chat volume, whether your microphone and your opponent's voice start live or muted, a voice style, and your speaker and microphone devices. See Settings and accessibility.
